source_text: μένων ἀγαθῶν. Ἐμαλακίσθη δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας, ἀπονεύσας εἰς αἰσχροκέρδειαν· ἐξ ἀνάνδρου δὲ τοῦτο καὶ ἀγεννοῦς λογισμοῦ· ταύτῃτοι καὶ ἄγευστος τῶν παρὰ Θεοῦ μεμένηκεν ἀγαθῶν, καὶ ἀμέτοχος παντελῶς τῶν τοῖς ἁγίοις δεδωρημένων. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὧδε ἔχει. {ΚΥΡ.} Καὶ θυσίας μὲν τῆς ἐξ ἀγέλης, οὗτος ὁ νόμος· τρόπῳ γε μὴν ἑτέρῳ, τὴν ἐξ ἱεροῦ προσάγεσθαι γένους προστέταχε λέγων· «Τοῦτο τὸ δῶρον Ἀαρὼν καὶ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ, ὃ προσοίσουσι Κυρίῳ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ ἂν χρίσῃς αὐτὸν, τὸ δέκατον τοῦ οἰφὶ σεμιδάλεως εἰς θυσίαν διαπαντὸς, τὸ ἥμισυ αὐτῆς τοπρωῒ, καὶ τὸ ἥμισυ αὐτῆς τὸ δειλινόν. Ἐπὶ τηγάνου ἐν ἐλαίῳ ποιηθήσεται· πεφυραμένην οἴσει αὐτὴν, ἑλικτὰ, θυσίαν ἐκ κλασμάτων, θυσίαν εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ. Ὁ ἱερεὺς ὁ χριστὸς ὁ ἀντ' αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ, ποιήσει αὐτήν· νόμος αἰώνιος, ἅπαν ἐπιτελεσθήσεται· καὶ πᾶσα θυσία ἱερέως ὁλόκαυτος ἔσται, καὶ οὐ βρωθήσεται.» Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τοῦ νόμου τὸ ἀκριβὲς, καὶ τὸ ἄγαν ἰσχνὸν εἰς ἀσφάλειαν ἱεροπρεπῆ. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ τὰς τῶν ἀγελαίων θυσίας οὐχ ὁλοκαυτοῦσθαι δεῖν προστέταχεν, ἅτε δὴ μὴ εἰσάπαν ἁγίαν ἐχόντων ζωὴν, μεμερισμένην δὲ ὥσπερ Θεῷ καὶ κόσμῳ, διιστὰς εἰκότως, καὶ ἐν μοίρᾳ τιθεὶς τῇ ὑπερκειμένῃ τοὺς ἐξειλεγμένους εἰς ἱερουργίαν, ὁλόκαυτον τὴν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ποιεῖσθαι δεῖν ἔφη θυσίαν, τὴν προσαγομένην σεμίδαλιν καταθυμιῶντας Θεῷ πρωῒ καὶ τὸ δειλινὸν, τοῦτ' ἔστι, διὰ πάσης ἡμέρας καὶ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ. Ἅγιος γὰρ ἀεί πώς ἐστι καὶ ἀκατάληκτον ἔχων τὴν εὐωδίαν, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τὴν πνευματικὴν, ὁ ἐξειλεγμένος, οὐ μεμερισμένος Θεῷ τε καὶ κόσμῳ, κατά τινας, εὐπαρέδρως δὲ καὶ ἀπερισπάστως, καὶ ὅλος ἐξ ὅλου προσκείμενος τῷ ἰδίῳ Δεσπότῃ, καὶ οἱονείπως ἀναβοῶν· «Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι, ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός.» Τὸ τοίνυν δέκατον τῆς σεμιδάλεως, ζωῆς ἂν εἴη σημεῖον, εὐωδιαζούσης Θεῷ κατὰ πάντα καιρόν. Ἀλλ' «ἐπὶ τηγάνου,» φησὶ, καὶ μὴν «καὶ ἐλαίῳ πεφυραμένην, καὶ ἐκ κλασμάτων ἀνοίσει αὐτήν·» τοῦ μὲν τηγάνου, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, τὸ ἐπώδυνον, τοῦ δὲ πεφυρᾶσθαι τῷ ἐλαίῳ, τὸ δαψιλὲς ἐν ἱλαρότητι, τοῦ δὲ ἐκ κλασμάτων, τὸ οἱονεὶ τρυφερόν τε καὶ εὐδιάθρυπτον τῆς τῶν ἁγίων καρδίας ὑποσημαινόντων ἡμῖν αἰνιγματωδῶς. Ἕψεται γὰρ πάντως τῇ εἰσάπαν καὶ ὁλοκλήρως ἁγίᾳ ζωῇ, τὸ ἐν πόνοις δεῖν εἶναι, καὶ τὸ ἀμφιλαφὲς ἐν ἐλπίδι τῇ παρὰ Θεῷ, καὶ τὸ εὐδιάθρυπτον κομιδῇ· πρέπει γὰρ ἂν ἥκιστά γε τὸ ἀτριβές. Γέγραπται γὰρ, ὅτι «Καρδίαν συντετριμμένην καὶ τεταπεινωμένην ὁ Θεὸς οὐκ ἐξουδενώσει.» Πέπηγε δὲ ὡς λίθος, καὶ ὥσπερ ἄκμων ἀνήλατος, ἡ τοῦ διαβόλου καρδία· λέγει γὰρ οὕτω τὸ Γράμμα τὸ ἱερόν. Ἐκτείνεται δὲ καὶ μέχρι παντὸς ὁ νόμος, ταῖς τῶν ἱερατευόντων διαδοχαῖς πληρούμενος· ἕπεσθαι γὰρ δεῖ ταῖς τῶν προλαβόν
pass_a_gloss: CYR: [col. 828: good things (ἀγαθῶν) — rendered in sec. 23.] Was softened (ἐμαλακίσθη) also Judas, having inclined away (ἀπονεύσας) into shameful gain (αἰσχροκέρδειαν); this from unmanly (ἀνάνδρου) and ignoble (ἀγεννοῦς) reasoning (λογισμοῦ); therefore he has remained untasting (ἄγευστος) of the goods from God and wholly unsharing (ἀμέτοχος) of the things given (δεδωρημένων) to the saints. PALL: thus it holds. CYR: and of the offering from the herd/flock (ἐξ ἀγέλης) this the law; but in another manner he has commanded the [offering] from sacred race (ἱεροῦ γένους) to be brought, saying: this the gift (δῶρον) of Aaron and his sons, which they will bring to Lord on the day on which you anoint (χρίσῃς) him: the tenth of the ephah (οἰφί) of fine flour for offering perpetually (διαπαντός), the half of it in the morning and the half in the evening (δειλινόν). On a pan (τηγάνου) in oil it will be made; kneaded (πεφυραμένην) he will bring it, rolled (ἑλικτά), offering of fragments (κλασμάτων), offering for odor of fragrance to Lord. The priest the anointed (ὁ χριστός) who [is] in place of him from his sons will make it; law eternal; all will be completed (ἐπιτελεσθήσεται); and every offering of priest will be whole burnt (ὁλόκαυτος) and will not be eaten [Lev 6:20-23 Eng. = LXX 6:13-16]. Look at (ἄθρει), O Palladius, the exactness (ἀκριβές) of the law and the very fine/subtle (ἰσχνόν) unto sacred befitting safety (ἀσφάλειαν). Since the offerings of the herd people (ἀγελαίων) he commanded must not be whole burnt, as not having entirely holy life but divided as it were to God and world, distinguishing (διιστάς) fittingly, and placing in the superior lot (μοίρᾳ ὑπερκειμένῃ) those chosen for sacred work, he said the [offering] for them must be made whole burnt, burning as incense (καταθυμιῶντας) the brought fine flour to God morning and evening, that is, through every day and in every season (καιρῷ). For holy always somehow is and having unceasing fragrance, clearly the spiritual, the chosen one, not divided to God and world, as some, but assiduously (εὐπαρέδρως) and undistractedly (ἀπερισπάστως), and whole from whole (ὅλος ἐξ ὅλου) attached (προσκείμενος) to his own Master (Δεσπότῃ), and as it were crying out: with Christ I have been co crucified, and I live no longer, but Christ lives in me [Gal 2:20]. The tenth then of the fine flour would be sign of life giving fragrance to God in every season. But on a pan, he says, and kneaded with oil, and from fragments he will bring it: the pan, as I think, the painful (ἐπώδυνον); the kneaded with oil, the abundance (δαψιλές) in cheerfulness (ἱλαρότητι); the from fragments, the as it were tender (τρυφερόν) and easily broken (εὐδιάθρυπτον) of the heart of the saints — signifying (ὑποσημαινόντων) to us riddlingly (αἰνιγματωδῶς). For there will wholly follow the entirely and wholly holy life the being in toils (πόνοις), and the abundance (ἀμφιλαφές) in hope with God, and the very easily broken; for least would befit the unworn/unbroken (ἀτριβές). For written: a heart crushed (συντετριμμένην) and humbled God will not despise (ἐξουδενώσει) [Ps 50:19 LXX]. Fixed (πέπηγε) as stone and as anvil (ἄκμων) unbeaten (ἀνήλατος) the heart of the devil; for so says the sacred Writing (Γράμμα) [Job 41:16 LXX]. The law extends even unto all [time], fulfilled by the successions (διαδοχαῖς) of those serving as priests; for one must follow the [good reputations? — continues col. 829] of those who went before (προλαβόν-[των]).
pass_b_english: Cyril: Judas too grew soft, and turned aside to greed for shameful gain; and this came from an unmanly and ignoble way of thinking. That is why he has remained without any taste of the good things that come from God, and wholly without share in the gifts given to the saints.

Cyril: This, then, is the law for the offering from the common flock. But he commanded that the offering from the priestly race be brought in another way, saying: ‘This is the gift of Aaron and his sons, which they shall offer to the Lord on the day when you anoint him: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a perpetual grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening. It shall be made with oil in a pan; he shall bring it kneaded, in rolls, a grain offering of broken pieces, a grain offering for a fragrant odor to the Lord. The anointed priest who succeeds him from among his sons shall make it. It is a perpetual law; all of it shall be offered. And every grain offering of a priest shall be wholly burnt; it shall not be eaten’ (Leviticus 6:20–23). See, Palladius, how exact the law is, and how finely it provides for the safety proper to holy things. Since he commanded that the offerings of the common flock should not be wholly burnt, because these people do not have a life that is entirely holy, but one divided, as it were, between God and the world, he rightly makes a distinction: he places those chosen for sacred service in the higher rank, and says that the offering made for them must be wholly burnt, as they burn to God as incense the fine flour that is brought, morning and evening, that is, through the whole day and at every season. For the chosen man is always, in some sense, holy, and has a fragrance that never ceases, a spiritual one, clearly. He is not divided between God and the world, as some are, but is in constant attendance and without distraction (1 Corinthians 7:35), wholly and entirely devoted to his own Master, and crying out, as it were: ‘I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me’ (Galatians 2:20). The tenth of the fine flour, then, would be a sign of a life that gives off fragrance to God at every season. But ‘in a pan,’ he says, and ‘kneaded with oil,’ and ‘he shall bring it in broken pieces’ (Leviticus 6:21). In a veiled way these signify to us: the pan, I think, what is painful; the kneading with oil, abundance joined with cheerfulness; the broken pieces, the tender and, so to speak, easily broken heart of the saints. For the life that is entirely and wholly holy will surely have to be lived amid toils, will have abundant hope in God, and will have a heart very easily broken; for hardness would least befit it. For it is written: ‘A broken and humbled heart God will not despise’ (Psalm 51:17). But the devil’s heart is set fast like a stone, and like an anvil that cannot be beaten (Job 41:24), for so Holy Scripture says. The law also extends through all time, fulfilled in the succession of those who serve as priests; for one must follow…

choices.why: ἀγέλη / ἀγελαῖοι (‘the flock’, ‘those of the flock’) here means the general body of the people as opposed to the priestly race (ἱερὸν γένος), not animal offerings; rendered ‘the common flock’.

Lev 6:20–23 English = LXX 6:13–16; ἑλικτά rendered ‘in rolls’, θυσία ἐκ κλασμάτων ‘a grain offering of broken pieces’, ὁ ἱερεὺς ὁ χριστός ‘the anointed priest’ (lower-case: Aaron’s successor, not Christ).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

PG 68.828. The first word of this column (ἀγαθῶν) is rendered at the end of section 23. Judas’s ‘shameful gain’ may recall John 12:6 but quotes nothing; uncited. ἀγέλη / ἀγελαῖοι (‘the flock’, ‘those of the flock’) here means the general body of the people as opposed to the priestly race (ἱερὸν γένος), not animal offerings; rendered ‘the common flock’. Lev 6:20–23 English = LXX 6:13–16; ἑλικτά rendered ‘in rolls’, θυσία ἐκ κλασμάτων ‘a grain offering of broken pieces’, ὁ ἱερεὺς ὁ χριστός ‘the anointed priest’ (lower-case: Aaron’s successor, not Christ). εὐπαρέδρως καὶ ἀπερισπάστως is the wording of 1 Cor 7:35 (literally ‘assiduously and undistractedly’); ‘serves’ carries the sense of εὐπάρεδρος (‘sitting constantly beside’), with no object added. Galatians 2:20 uses common English numbering (NA28 places ‘I have been crucified with Christ’ at 2:19). Psalm 51:17 = LXX Psalm 50:19. ‘The devil’s heart … like an anvil that cannot be beaten’ is LXX Job 41:15–16 (Rahlfs 41:16), said there of the dragon/Leviathan, which Cyril reads as the devil; English Bible numbering Job 41:24 (Hebrew 41:16). ‘Hardness’ renders τὸ ἀτριβές (‘the unworn, unbroken’). The section ends mid-sentence (προλαβόν-); ‘those who went before’ is rendered here and the noun that follows belongs to section 25.

changes: αἰσχροκέρδεια: ‘greed for shameful gain’; μεμένηκεν ‘has remained without any taste’
Lev 6:20–23 (= LXX 6:13–16) checked; ‘a tenth’, ἅπαν ἐπιτελεσθήσεται ‘all of it shall be offered’
Modality fix: οὐχ … δεῖν ‘should not be wholly burnt’ (draft ‘need not’ weakened the command); ἐπειδή … διιστάς … ἔφη structure restored
Θεῷ moved to καταθυμιῶντας (‘burn to God as incense’), not ‘brought before God’
εὐπαρέδρως: ‘in constant attendance’ (drops added ‘serves’), ὅλος ἐξ ὅλου ‘wholly and entirely’
Added Lev 6:21 for repeated pan/oil/pieces quotation; ‘In a riddle’ → ‘In a veiled way’; restored γάρ before ‘hardness’
